extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties in PTAB inter partes review proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, and their counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: An inter partes review (IPR) institution decision from the Patent Trial and Appeal Board explaining legal standards and applying them to determine whether to institute review of challenged patent claims. Covers institution standard, claim construction, obviousness analysis, multiple-petition and parallel-litigation discretion, and related procedural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution of an inter partes review is authorized when 'the information presented in the petition . . . and any response . . . shows that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the petition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the threshold for institution at the preliminary stage; the Board determines whether the petition (and any response) demonstrates a reasonable likelihood the petitioner would prevail on at least one challenged claim. The inquiry is based on the current record and is preliminary, not a final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's burden to show unpatentability with particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: In an inter partes review, the petitioner has the burden from the onset to show with particularity why the patent it challenges is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Harmonic Inc. v. Avid Tech. and 35 U.S.C. § 312(a)(3). At institution the petitioner must present particularized arguments and evidence (e.g., declarations, argument mapping claim elements to references). Lack of particularity can defeat the petition at institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness legal standard (KSR / Graham framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim is unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) if differences between the claimed subject matter and the prior art are such that the subject matter would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve obviousness based on underlying factual determinations: (1) scope and content of the prior art; (2) differences between the claim and the prior art; (3) the level of ordinary skill in the art; and (4) objective evidence of nonobviousness (secondary considerations). Apply KSR's teaching, suggestion, or motivation and reasoned explanation, including motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of ordinary skill in the art (LOSITA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the person of ordinary skill in the art for the claimed subject matter; example here: 'would have had a B.S. degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or an equivalent field, as well as at least 2-3 years of academic or industry experience in computer networking and digital advertising, or comparable industry experience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may propose differing definitions; Board may adopt a party's proposed level if consistent with the prior art of record. The Board notes that more experience can compensate for less formal education and vice versa. LOSITA is a factual input to the obviousness analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard (37 C.F.R. § 42.100(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim 'shall be construed using the same claim construction standard that would be used to construe the claim in a civil action under 35 U.S.C. § 282(b).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is ordinary and customary meaning; parties can argue specific constructions. The Board may adopt constructions used by a district court in related litigation for purposes of institution, but such constructions are preliminary and the parties may develop the record further during trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt district court constructions preliminarily where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: For claim construction at institution, the Board may apply a construction issued by a district court in related litigation (here, the District Court's construction of 'situational network' as 'a network created in response to an event or situation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such adoption is preliminary for institution purposes. The Board encourages parties to further develop the record at trial if they object or wish to refine constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and interpretation of specific claim terms (example: 'situational network')
rubrics_metrics.description: Example construction applied: 'situational network' = 'a network created in response to an event or situation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will interpret claim language consistent with the specification and prior constructions where appropriate. Parties' alternative constructions and related litigation constructions are considered; the Board notes the construction's preliminary nature and invites further record development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping claim limitations to prior art and combination rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: To show unpatentability, the petitioner must map each claimed limitation to disclosures in the prior art and, when relying on combinations, explain why a person of ordinary skill would have been motivated to combine references with a reasonable expectation of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board reviews cited passages, figures, and expert testimony (declarations) showing where each limitation is taught. Motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success may be supported by common industry practices and expert opinion. At institution, persuasive but preliminary showings are sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of expert declarations and evidence at institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner relies on expert declarations (e.g., Dr. Jansen) to support contentions such as teachings in prior art, motivation to combine, and ordinary skill level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert testimony is accepted as part of the record to establish factual elements at the institution stage. The Board considers such declarations in determining whether the petition shows a reasonable likelihood of prevailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble and whether limiting
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the claim preamble is limiting need not be decided at institution if parties have not argued it; the Board may proceed without resolving preamble limitingness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither party presents arguments that the preamble is limiting, the Board may find sufficient support for the preamble's content in the cited art without deciding the limiting question; such issues can be developed further at trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple petitions guidance (CTPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has indicated that 'one petition should be sufficient to challenge the claims of a patent in most situations,' but recognizes circumstances where more than one petition may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors: whether petitions are duplicative, whether they challenge substantially different claim scope, overlap of asserted prior art, burden on the Board and patent owner, and claim length. Overlap of prior art and claim differences can mitigate concerns that parallel petitions impose substantial unnecessary burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board discretion to deny institution for parallel district court litigation (Fintiv factors and Director's memorandum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Owner may request discretionary denial under Fintiv based on parallel district court litigation. The Director's June 21, 2022 Memorandum states the PTAB will not discretionarily deny institution where a petitioner presents a Sotera stipulation (not to pursue in district court the same grounds or those that reasonably could have been raised before the PTAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petitioner provides a Sotera stipulation, the Board generally will decline to exercise discretion to deny institution under Fintiv. The Board applies the guidance of the Director's memorandum when evaluating discretion in parallel proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art status and effective filing date considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether cited references qualify as prior art under the applicable statutory regime (here, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. § 103 because earliest possible effective filing date is before March 16, 2013) and whether references are §102(e) art based on their priority claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing prior art status (e.g., §102(e)) and priority can be essential to grounds; petitioner must show the references' applicability (e.g., priority to an earlier provisional) in the petition and supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution authorizes review on all challenged claims and grounds (37 C.F.R. § 42.108(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When instituting review, the Board will authorize the review to proceed on all of the challenged claims and on all grounds of unpatentability asserted for each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petitioner meets the institution threshold for at least one challenged claim and ground, the Board usually institutes on all challenged claims and grounds asserted in the petition; detailed contest on other claims may be left for trial after full record development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of arguments about timing of network formation and pre-existing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that a prior-art system's connections were formed prior to an event (e.g., user subscriptions) do not necessarily defeat a showing that a 'situational network' is established 'in response to' an event; the claim language may permit use of stored information to facilitate establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board examines whether the claim language requires the connections to be created only after the event or whether stored preferences may be used at the time of the event to form the situational network. At institution, Board found stored subscription data can be used to facilitate formation in response to an event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary vs. full-trial posture
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution decisions are preliminary determinations as to whether there is a reasonable likelihood of prevailing and do not resolve all factual or legal disputes; many issues are reserved for trial after full record development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings at institution are based on the current record and are meant to decide whether to proceed to trial, not to be final adjudications of patentability.
